summary.oneLiner: SPL Industries is a leading Indian exporter of knitted fabric and garments, operating one of the largest vertically integrated knitwear plants in India, serving US and European markets.
summary.business: SPL Industries Limited is a leading apparel export house and manufacturer of knitted fabric and knitted garments. The company operates a vertically integrated knitwear plant in India and is reputed for product development and design capability. It exports primarily to the United States and European markets, while also catering to the domestic market.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: SPL Industries is a leading Indian exporter of knitted fabric and garments, operating one of the largest vertically integrated knitwear plants in India, serving US and European markets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: SPL Industries Limited is a leading apparel export house and manufacturer of knitted fabric and knitted garments. The company operates a vertically integrated knitwear plant in India and is reputed for product development and design capability. It exports primarily to the United States and European markets, while also catering to the domestic market.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Abundant domestic cotton availability ensuring cost-efficiency and supply stability
- Favourable macroeconomic conditions with India GDP growth revised upward to 7.3%-7.4% supporting domestic consumption
- Government support through PLI scheme, Integrated Textile Programme, and dedicated Ministry of Textiles allocation
- Growing export opportunities from India-EU FTA (zero-duty access), India-UK and India-EFTA agreements enabling geographic diversification
- Continued United States tariff-related headwinds on Indian textile and apparel exports creating pricing pressures
- Subdued domestic and export demand and pricing pressures from steep US tariffs impacting income and profit

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Vertically integrated knitwear manufacturing and export with strong product development and design capability
- Long-term business diversification into real estate (object clause amended, no operations commenced)
- The provided annual-report text does not contain a dividend policy, payout, buyback, debt reduction, credit rating, or reinvestment intent statement.
- Global shift towards sustainable textiles: Increasing demand for eco-friendly and ethically produced products aligns with SPL's sustainability agenda.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY 2025–26, SPL Industries altered its Memorandum of Association to include real estate-related activities as part of a long-term business diversification strategy. No real estate operations commenced during the year, and the company's operations remained entirely in textiles. The company operates one of the largest vertically integrated knitwear plants in India, serving as a leading manufacturer and exporter of knitted fabric and garments. No new capex projects, capacity additions, or expansion timelines were disclosed for the textile segment.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vertically integrated operations from fabric to garment, providing cost and supply-chain control.
- Strong product development and design capability, attracting a strong international clientele.
- Abundant domestic raw material availability as India is the world's largest cotton producer, ensuring cost-efficiency and supply stability.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- US tariff headwinds on Indian textile and apparel exports — Steep US tariffs created pricing pressures and subdued export demand, directly reducing revenue and profit in FY26. Continued tariff uncertainty threatens a key export market.
- Subdued domestic and export demand for textiles — Challenging market conditions led to lower income and profit. Persistent demand weakness could further erode revenue and capacity utilization.
- Concentration in a single operating segment (garments) — The company operates entirely in the garment segment. Any sector-specific downturn or disruption leaves no revenue diversification buffer.
- Real estate diversification execution risk — The MoA was altered to include real estate activities, but no operations commenced. Entering an unrelated business carries capital allocation, execution, and regulatory risks without proven competence.
- No dividend payout and modest net worth growth — Retained earnings are the sole driver of net worth increase. Absence of dividends may signal limited cash returns to shareholders, and modest growth leaves less cushion against shocks.
- Dependence on government support schemes — Growth is partly premised on PLI, Integrated Textile Programme, and budget allocations. Any reduction or policy shift could weaken the supportive environment.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Vertically integrated knitwear manufacturing and export with strong product development and design capability
- Long-term business diversification into real estate (object clause amended, no operations commenced)
- The provided annual-report text does not contain a dividend policy, payout, buyback, debt reduction, credit rating, or reinvestment intent statement.
- Global shift towards sustainable textiles: Increasing demand for eco-friendly and ethically produced products aligns with SPL's sustainability agenda.
